# Herma

**Herma:** programmable AI request middleware for configurable coding harnesses — intercepts outbound LLM calls via keyword, semantic, and micromodel triggers to inject versioned rules, provisions, and URIs before model execution.

In Classical Greece, a *herma* was an inscribed roadside stone waymarker placed along the road, carved with civic precepts and directional pointers that travellers read *en route* to their destination. **Herma** sits inline between configurable agentic coding harnesses (`muse-code`, `opencode`, `claude-code`, `codex`, `swarm-worker`) and upstream LLM endpoints (`/v1/chat/completions`, `/v1/responses`, `/v1/messages`).

## Why Herma Exists

Static system prompts bloat every turn when stuffed with every rule in an organization, yet omitting a rule causes agents to violate subtle invariants. Herma loads versioned **provisions** and **URI pointers** from [Tessera](https://github.com/ta-amps/tessera) (or any remote handshake provision store) and evaluates a **three-tier trigger pipeline** on each outbound request:

1. **Tier 1 — Keyword, Regex, File-Path & Tool Triggers (`~0 ms`)**: Exact terms, bounded regexes, workspace file globs (`src/tessera/*.py`), and declared tool names.
2. **Tier 2 — Semantic Similarity Triggers (`~1–5 ms`)**: Hybrid concept-cluster + subword cosine matching (plus optional `/v1/embeddings`) so paraphrased intent fires the right provision even with zero shared literal keywords.
3. **Tier 3 — Micromodel Router Triggers**: Lightweight fast classifier prompt (`HERMA_MICROMODEL_URL`, with deterministic offline fallback) invoked only when Tier 1 and Tier 2 did not already match in `any` mode.

Matched provisions inject bounded rule prose and authoritative URIs (`https://`, `tessera://blobs/<sha256>`, `tessera://buckets/<bucket>/<key>`, `mcp://`, `urn:`) once per conversation (skipping duplicate re-injection on later turns) and record a canonical SHA-256 `InjectionReceipt`.

## Configurable Coding Harnesses Only

Herma is intentionally restricted to **fully configurable agentic coding harnesses** where the developer controls custom base URLs, headers, and scoped `hmk_<id>.<secret>` credentials:
- Supported harnesses: `muse-code`, `opencode`, `claude-code`, `codex`, `swarm-worker`, `custom-harness`.
- Closed consumer chat clients (such as a generic **Muse Personal Assistant** chat session, browser navigation requests, or cookie sessions) cannot configure provisions or route through Herma (`HTTP 403 harness_required`).
- Contributor-tier models (`*-contributor`) are deterministically refused (`HTTP 403 contributor_tier_refused`).

## Quick Start

```bash
git clone https://github.com/ta-amps/tessera.git
git clone https://github.com/ta-amps/herma.git
cd herma
make setup
make check
make demo
```

# Summary

**Herma** is a programmable middle-layer proxy for configurable AI coding harnesses. Before an outbound LLM request reaches `/v1/chat/completions`, `/v1/responses`, or `/v1/messages`, Herma:

1. Verifies the caller holds a scoped `hmk_` credential bound to a configurable coding harness (`muse-code`, `opencode`, `claude-code`, `codex`, `swarm-worker`, or `custom-harness`) and is not a closed consumer assistant.
2. Refuses `-contributor` model tiers so code and synthetic case fixtures stay in Standard mode.
3. Evaluates active versioned **provisions** loaded from SQLite, **Tessera** (`herma.provisions` CAS records + `tessera://blobs/<sha256>` excerpts), or a **remote handshake provision server** (`/v1/handshake` + `/v1/provisions`).
4. Runs **keyword/regex/path/tool** (`~0 ms`), **semantic** (`~1–5 ms`), and **micromodel** triggers, short-circuiting the micromodel whenever an earlier tier already matched in `any` mode.
5. Injects matched provision text and authoritative URIs within a bounded character budget, skips provisions already injected earlier in the same conversation (`once_per_conversation`), and records a SHA-256 `InjectionReceipt`.

# Architecture

Herma separates pure schema and trigger evaluation from storage, payload mutation, and HTTP edge lockdown:

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  H["Configurable Coding Harness<br/>muse-code / opencode / claude-code / codex"] --> E["Cloudflare Worker Edge<br/>x-edge-auth + HSTS/CSP"]
  E --> G["Harness Gate<br/>hmk_ scopes + consumer refusal"]
  G --> T["3-Tier Trigger Engine<br/>1. Keyword  2. Semantic  3. Micromodel"]
  S[("SQLite WAL Store<br/>synced from Tessera or Remote Handshake")] --> T
  T --> I["Injector + Dedupe + Budget<br/>SHA-256 InjectionReceipt"]
  I --> U["Upstream LLM Endpoint<br/>/v1/chat/completions · /v1/responses · /v1/messages"]
```

## Components

- `herma/errors.py` — RFC 9457 `problem+json` error hierarchy.
- `herma/schemas.py` — strict Pydantic v2 models for provisions, URIs, triggers, harness keys, and receipts.
- `herma/harness_gate.py` — constant-time `hmk_` verification, consumer-surface refusal, `configure` harness attestation, and `-contributor` refusal.
- `herma/triggers/` — `keyword.py`, `semantic.py`, `micromodel.py`, and `engine.py`.
- `herma/store.py` — SQLite WAL store, compare-and-set updates, Tessera CAS/blob sync, and remote handshake sync.
- `herma/injector.py` — multi-protocol envelope extraction, provision formatting, turn deduplication, and SHA-256 receipts.
- `herma/proxy.py` — upstream forwarding (JSON and streaming SSE) with allowlisted upstream hosts.
- `herma/api/` — FastAPI app (`:7730`) with `HERMA_EDGE_SECRET` lockdown and server-rendered read-only pages.

## Invariants

| Id | Always true | Checked by |
|---|---|---|
| H01 | Generic consumer chat assistants, browser navigation requests, and cookie-authenticated calls are deterministically refused | `test_consumer_assistant_and_browser_navigation_refused`, `test_http_edge_lockdown_and_dry_run_across_wire_formats` |
| H02 | Provision management and remote sync require both configure scope and explicit matching X-Herma-Harness attestation | `test_consumer_assistant_and_browser_navigation_refused`, `test_route_only_key_cannot_configure` |
| H03 | Contributor-tier models (-contributor) are refused across outbound LLM payloads and micromodel trigger classifiers | `test_tier3_micromodel_classifier_and_contributor_refusal`, `test_http_edge_lockdown_and_dry_run_across_wire_formats` |
| H04 | Tier-1 keyword, bounded regex, path-glob, and tool-name triggers match deterministically without network calls | `test_tier1_keyword_regex_path_and_tool_triggers` |
| H05 | Tier-2 semantic triggers match paraphrased intent without literal keyword overlap | `test_tier2_semantic_paraphrase_without_literal_id` |
| H06 | Tier-1 or Tier-2 hits short-circuit Tier-3 micromodel calls when trigger mode is any | `test_engine_short_circuits_micromodel_when_keyword_matches` |
| H07 | Compare-and-set versions prevent silent provision overwrites, Tessera blob URIs resolve deterministically, and remote handshakes clamp max_chars | `test_cas_conflict_and_tessera_blob_sync`, `test_remote_handshake_clamps_max_chars` |
| H08 | Multi-turn conversations deduplicate once_per_conversation provisions and HERMA_EDGE_SECRET blocks direct origin traffic lacking x-edge-auth | `test_http_edge_lockdown_and_dry_run_across_wire_formats` |

# Connecting Configurable Agentic Coding Harnesses

Herma accepts requests **only** from configurable agentic coding harnesses that support custom provider endpoints, custom headers, and scoped `hmk_` credentials.

## 1. Issue a Key

```bash
uv run herma keys issue --label workstation --harness opencode --scopes route,configure
```

Save the printed `hmk_<id>.<secret>` token in a `0600` secret file.

## 2. OpenCode / OpenAI-Compatible Harnesses (`/v1/chat/completions`)

Point your provider `baseURL` at `https://herma.ta-amps.workers.dev/v1` (or `http://127.0.0.1:7730/v1` locally) and attach:
- `X-Herma-Key: hmk_<id>.<secret>`
- `X-Herma-Harness: opencode`
- `X-Upstream-Api-Key: <your-upstream-llm-key>` (or set `HERMA_UPSTREAM_API_KEY` on the Herma origin)

## 3. Muse Code / Responses-Compatible Harnesses (`/v1/responses`)

Point the Responses endpoint at `https://herma.ta-amps.workers.dev/v1/responses` with `X-Herma-Harness: muse-code` and `--contributor-mode off`. Herma injects matched provisions directly into `instructions`.

## 4. Claude Code (`/v1/messages`)

Set `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL=https://herma.ta-amps.workers.dev` and pass `X-Herma-Key` + `X-Herma-Harness: claude-code` via custom headers. Herma injects matched provisions into the top-level `system` prompt.

## Why Generic Consumer Assistants Cannot Access Herma

Locked consumer chat apps (such as a generic **Muse Personal Assistant** session on web/mobile) cannot set custom proxy base URLs, cannot attach `X-Herma-Key` / `X-Herma-Harness` headers, and are explicitly blocked by `herma/harness_gate.py` (`HTTP 403 harness_required`).

# Setup, Backing Stores & Cloudflare Deployment

## Local Development

```bash
make setup
make check
make demo
uv run herma serve --host 127.0.0.1 --port 7730
```

## Syncing Provisions from Backing Stores

1. **Tessera (`herma.provisions` + `provisions` bucket)**:
   - Local Python store: `store.publish_to_tessera_store(t_store)` and `store.sync_from_tessera_store(t_store)`.
   - Over HTTP or Cloudflare Service Binding: `POST /v1/sync/tessera` with `{"base_url": "https://tessera.ta-amps.workers.dev", "bearer_token": "..."}`. Content-addressed `tessera://blobs/<sha256>` and bucket-backed `tessera://buckets/<bucket>/<key>` URIs have their excerpts resolved automatically.
2. **Remote Handshake Provision Server**:
   - `POST /v1/sync/remote` negotiates version and clamped `max_chars` via `POST /v1/handshake` (passing configurable `surface_header` + `surface_id`) before loading `/v1/provisions`.

## Deploying on Cloudflare `workers.dev` (24/7 Cloud-Persistent Mode)

`deploy/cloudflare/wrangler.jsonc` runs natively in Cloudflare's cloud (`STORAGE_MODE = "cloud"`) backed by the `ta-amps-herma` D1 database (`HERMA_DB`) and a direct `TESSERA` Service Binding (`deploy/cloudflare/d1-herma.sql`), or proxies to an external `ORIGIN` when `STORAGE_MODE = "proxy"`:

```bash
npx --yes wrangler@4.149.0 d1 execute ta-amps-herma --remote --file deploy/cloudflare/d1-herma.sql --config deploy/cloudflare/wrangler.jsonc -y
npx --yes wrangler@4.149.0 deploy --config deploy/cloudflare/wrangler.jsonc
npx --yes wrangler@4.149.0 secret put BOOTSTRAP_SECRET --config deploy/cloudflare/wrangler.jsonc < /path/to/bootstrap.secret
```

# Example Provisions

Each JSON file in this folder conforms to `herma.schemas.Provision` (`extra="forbid"`):

- `PROV-TESSERA-FENCING.json` — Tier-1 keyword/path/tool + Tier-2 semantic trigger for atomic lease fencing and CAS writes.
- `PROV-SHAMASH-NON-ACCUSATORY.json` — Tier-1 keyword/path + Tier-2 semantic trigger enforcing non-accusatory risk indicators and `SYNTHETIC` bundle checks.
- `PROV-NGO-HUMAN-BOUNDARY.json` — Tier-3 micromodel classifier trigger enforcing `human_only` crisis boundaries and `drafter != reviewer`.
- `PROV-EDGE-ORIGIN-LOCKDOWN.json` — Tier-1 keyword/path trigger enforcing `x-edge-auth` (`EDGE_SECRET`), cookie stripping, HSTS, and CSP on Cloudflare Workers.

# Handoff & Status

- **Built & Verified (`v0.1.0`)**:
  - Strict Pydantic v2 schemas (`Provision`, `ProvisionURI`, `KeywordTrigger`, `SemanticTrigger`, `MicromodelTrigger`, `InjectionReceipt`).
  - Configurable-harness gate (`hmk_` SHA-256 hashed credentials, `route` vs. `configure` scopes, consumer-assistant refusal, `-contributor` model refusal).
  - 3-tier trigger engine with `any`/`all` composition and Tier-3 short-circuiting.
  - Multi-protocol request augmentation (`/v1/chat/completions`, `/v1/responses`, `/v1/messages`, `/v1/dry-run`) with `once_per_conversation` deduplication and character budgets.
  - SQLite WAL store + Tessera CAS/blob sync + remote handshake provision sync.
  - Cloudflare Worker edge (`deploy/cloudflare/`) + scale-to-zero Fly config (`deploy/fly/`).
- **Next Extensions**:
  - Per-repository rule-pack signature verification (Ed25519) on remote handshake bundles.
  - Streaming token-usage accounting attached to `InjectionReceipt`.

# AGENTS.md — Herma Hard Rules

1. **Configurable Harnesses Only**: Never weaken `herma/harness_gate.py`. Provision management (`configure` scope) and request interception (`route` scope) require scoped `hmk_` credentials and reject generic consumer chat surfaces (such as Muse Personal Assistant), browser navigation, and cookie auth.
2. **Standard Mode Only**: Refuse every `-contributor` model ID in both outbound proxy payloads and micromodel classifier configs (`ContributorTierRefusedError`).
3. **Domain-Neutral Core**: Keep `herma/` domain-neutral. Specific project provisions belong in `examples/provisions/*.json`, Tessera stores (`herma.provisions`), or remote handshake stores.
4. **Public Repo Hygiene**: Run `make check` (`ruff`, `mypy --strict`, `pytest`, `check_public.py`, `build_index.py --check`, `check_architecture.py`) before every commit. Never include secrets, tokens, or private names.
5. **Git Identity**: Commit as `ta-amps <348409696+ta-amps@users.noreply.github.com>` with zero `Co-Authored-By` trailers.
